rationale: FPT/GHEC/GHES permissions metadata permits repository writers to publish to that repository in the documented flow; actual registry credentials/scopes, feature availability and package access remain separately required, not implied by repository write alone. Package description and installation/usage instructions help consumers; version metadata includes publication date, downloads and recent versions. The example external package is illustrative, not an executed receipt or fully reviewed independent artifact. The public/private reusable describes repository-linked sharing with all GitHub users on FPT/GHEC versus everyone in the enterprise on GHES, or private collaborators/organization. Qualify this description against granular-registry separate visibility rules rather than flattening repository visibility into package visibility. One repository can connect to several packages; the source asks that README and description distinguish each. Documentation clarity is a recommendation/intent, not proof of complete package linkage or a universal one-package architecture. FPT/GHEC fixes of a vulnerability should be accompanied by a repository security advisory. GitHub reviews published advisories and may generate Dependabot alerts for affected repositories; an advisory does not guarantee alerts or verified downstream remediation, and the conditional is not asserted for GHES. The publishing tutorial uses a classic PAT with task-appropriate scopes and client-specific authentication/publishing instructions. It does not authorize creating tokens, broaden scopes by default, or negate separately documented workflow GITHUB_TOKEN publication support. FPT/GHEC supported clients versus GHES instance-enabled package types limit the procedure. GHEC managed-user namespace constraints and registry-specific limits remain; published-page navigation after a publish is not effective-access, rights, security or native enforcement evidence. GHES release-stage include is only a comment, not a feature-disable rule. No package published, source commands executed or new credentials created; outbound token, registry, advisory and viewing guides remain separately scoped and no policy/rights acceptance follows. Full file and required includes read; candidate accounting does not independently certify extraction completeness or published assurance.
